title: Delta acquires 100% of Echo – one year later
text: On 31 December N, Delta acquired 100% of Echo for 1,200 in cash. At that date Echo's equity was 800 (share capital). Echo's equipment had a fair value 100 above its carrying amount (remaining useful life 5 years, straight-line), and Echo had an internally developed brand name with a fair value of 150 (indefinite useful life).
At 31 December N1 the brand name is impaired: its recoverable amount is 120. Goodwill is not impaired.

title: Max GmbH – impairment and reversal of a machine
text: Max acquired a machine on 1 January N1 for €500,000; useful life 10 years, no residual value, straight-line depreciation, cost model.
At the end of N2 a competitor launches a much more efficient technology (indication of impairment): fair value less costs to sell €300,000, value in use €320,000.
At the end of N3 Max wins a long-term exclusive contract using the machine (indication of reversal): recoverable amount €380,000. The remaining useful life is unchanged.

title: Lease or service?
text: Contract 1: A retailer rents a specified store unit in a shopping centre for 6 years. It decides on the assortment, opening hours within the centre's rules and the shop design.
Contract 2: A company buys 'storage capacity of 500 TB' from a data-centre provider. The provider can move the data to any of its servers at any time and decides how the servers are operated.
Contract 3 (store unit): payments of €50,000 at the beginning of each year for 3 years (first payment at commencement), interest rate 6%, annuity factor (6%, 2 years) = 1.8334.
